title: "Monster force"

Electrical interactions are monstrously strong. A typical elephant's mass is
roughly one billion times a typical ant's mass. By comparison, the electrical
attraction between an electron and a proton is 10^40^ times the gravitational
attraction between an electron and a proton. If you're like me, you simply can't
imagine a difference in strength between forces of scale 10^40^
(ten-thousand-billion-billion-billion times). You'd likely think the electrical
force would always drown the gravitational force.

A very interesting difference between electrical and gravitational forces is
that gravitational interactions are only attractive whereas electrical
interactions can either be attractive or repulsive (like charges repel and
unlike charges attract). Consequently, the gravitation interaction between the
constituents of our bodies and the constituents of the earth adds-up, whereas
the electrical interactions between the constituents of our bodies and the
constituents of the earth cancels-out. Thus, overall, we actually notice the
earth's pull from the factor-10^40^ weaker gravitational force rather than the
factor-10^40^ stronger electric force. In this sense, electricity is the monster
that is hidden under the bed, with neutral objects being chockablock full of
electric charge and electric force.

Coulomb's law is the quantitative description of the electric force F**~E~**
between two charges q~1~, q~2~ with a separation **r**. Coulomb's law for the
electric force between two charges echoes Newton's law for the gravitational
force between two masses. Both laws are inverse square laws, i.e., at twice the
separation both forces are four times weaker. Both forces are interaction
between dimensions of nature, i.e., mass in the case of gravity and charge in
the case of electricity. And both forces are exerted along the line joining the
two interacting masses or two interaction charges (we call such forces central
forces).

Note the 'fact' that electrons are negatively charged and protons are positively
charged is purely convention. We could the define the charge of electrons to be
negative and the charge of protons to be positive and the universe would be
unchanged. All that matters is electrons and protons have opposite charges and
that unlike-charges attract and like-charges repel.

In considering the description of the interaction between two charges, the
vector displacement is the vector from one charge to the other charge. Since the
interaction only 'knows' this direction the interaction can only act along this
direction. Attraction and repulsion are the two options for a force acting along
the line between two charges.

Newton's law for the gravitational force and Coulomb's law for the electric
force have forms so similar its tempting to imagine a common mechanism for both
forces. But actually we'll discover that's incorrect. To understand gravity
we'll need to expand our understanding of space and time.

Coulomb was a mechanical engineer with a keen interest in electricity, a very
serendipitous mix for his development of the torsion balance experiment. His
torsion balance measurements - that uncovered the detailed workings of
electrical interactions between electric charges - were an experimental
masterpiece and a befitting culmination for the two thousand year journey from
the first notions of mysterious attractions (600BC) to the final description of
the electric force (1785).

Torsion and tension are cousins. If you pull the opposite ends of a wire in
opposite directions the wire resists - that's tension. If you twist the opposite
ends of a wire in opposite directions the wire resists - that's torsion. You can
utilize such reactions to measure an unknown force or torque by balancing the
unknown force or torque with the tension or the torsion of a calibrated wire (by
calibrated I mean a given stretch / twist corresponds to a known force /
torque). One difference between the tension and the torsion of a wire is that a
large force is typically needed to significantly stretch a wire but a small
torque is sufficient to significantly twist a wire. Thus torsion balances are
good for measuring tiny forces. The torsion balance was famously used by both
Cavendish to determine the tiny gravitational interaction between two massive
spheres and Coulomb to measure the electrical interaction between two charged
spheres. And today they're actually used to search for new forces of nature.

Like the gravitational force is the origin of the solar system, the electric
force is the origin of the atomic system. The very different scales of the solar
and atomic systems is a reflection of the very different strengths of the
gravitational and electrical forces. However, the fact that gravity and
electricity are both central, inverse-square law forces, has an common imprint
on the orbit motion of the planets and the electrons. As humans, we're made from
the world of the electrical force and reside in the world of the gravitational
force.

Coulomb's law only describes the problem of forces between pairs of charges. To
solve problems of three, four or more charges we need to supplement the law with
the superposition principle. The principle states that the net force on a
electric charge due to neighboring charges is the vector sum of the individual
forces of the neighboring charges, **F** = **F~1~** + **F~2~** +..... (be aware
that forces are vectors).

The superposition principle, while experimental fact, isn't entirely obvious.
Think about human relationships; your interaction with your Mom or your friend
is likely different when it's just the two of you from when you're among a
group. This isn't the case for electric forces; the interaction of q~2~ with
q~1~ is unaffected by nearby q~3~. We'll discover that superposition was
actually a clue to the detailed mechanism of the electric interaction.

As hinted, in applying the superposition of forces we'll use vector addition
(you'll remember that vectors are quantities with magnitude and direction). In
class we'll review the procedures for adding vectors by disassembling them into
x,y components - metaphorically cleaving space into one-dimensional pieces where
the complicated addition of vectors is replaced by ordinary addition of
numbers.^3^ As an example of superposition of forces we'll consider the question
of why matter is bound together given being assembled from equal numbers of
positively and negatively charges that cause repulsive and attractive electric
forces. The secret to stability is unlike charges being closer together, and
like charges being farther apart, and therefore the attractive forces overcoming
the repulsive forces.

As an example, consider a sodium chloride nano-crystal consisting of two Na+
ions and two Cl- ions. The ions are located at the corners of a square with
like-ions at opposite corners (e.g., the Na ions at the top-right and the
bottom-left and the Cl ions at the other corners). In such an arrangement all
ions will experience a force that acts towards the crystal's center. These
forces are the combination of the stronger attractive forces of the
nearest-neighbors, opposite-sign ions and the weaker repulsive force of the
opposite corner, same-sign ions. These cohesive forces will pull together the
charged ions and thereby bind the nano-crystal (and macroscopic-sized crystals).

Next time you shake salt on your boiled egg or your french fries take a look at
a salt crystal. A typical crystal is roughly 10^18^ atoms. Within the crystal is
a cubic lattice of positive Na ions and negative Cl ions that outshines any
human construction. A vast, 3-dimensional 'patio' of Na / Cl building blocks.
Now take a look at the salt shaker. It contains roughly one million
three-dimensional 'patios' of Na / Cl building blocks. Nature is breathtaking -
when you take the time to look.
